blocks.A: Foundation: from existence to the finite carrier
blocks.C: The Subject: the frame and its registration
blocks.G: Interactions: electromagnetism, the weak and strong forces, matter, flavour and superconductivity
blocks.P: Predictions (the master's falsifiable exposures; the papers' P blocks carry theirs)
blocks.T: Tasks: the development roadmap (stated surfaces, proofs or executions outstanding)
blocks.Y: Conjectures (stated ahead of derivation; promotion re-homes a row in its thematic block)
blocks.Z: The horizon (the limits of the bounded observer)

tags.G: ground — the single given that conditions the discourse
tags.D: definition — a naming or set-up move, no empirical content
tags.R: realisation — what a physical term denotes in the substrate; forced (A9), each row stating the falsifier that kills it
tags.I: import — a standard result or measured datum, used without reproof
tags.Ω: Ω-hard — a value in no embedded reader's window, not closeable by a bounded observer; host-decided on any laboratory Carrier; never applied to a relation

rows.label: A1
rows.name: The Universe exists
rows.statement: \textbf{The Universe exists}: the sole indubitable given (``I think, therefore the Universe is''). Neither axiom nor assumption.

rows.label: A2
rows.name: Finitude
rows.statement: \textbf{Finitude}: the totality is finite, a count of $\Om$ elements. Infinity as an ontological posit is incoherent (no model is exhibited; the completed totality forbids its own totality as an object; its consistency is unprovable within, 5-red Prop.~9), unverifiable (idleness, 29-fin) and redundant (every certificate is finite, 5-red).

rows.label: A3
rows.name: Completeness
rows.statement: \textbf{Completeness}: the totality has no outside, so whatever exists is a part of it, and it has no host. It is unique, since two totalities would each lie within the other. Observers are shells embedded \emph{within}, not parallel carriers.

rows.label: A4
rows.name: A bounded observer is a proper part
rows.statement: A bounded observer is a proper part, $|O|<\Om$: by A2 and A5 its states are fewer than the totality's, so no injective encoding of the totality into its states exists (25:D1, 5:C2); every reading $\Pi_i{:}\Om\to\mathcal D_i$ is an incomplete projection, its image strictly smaller than the whole. The limitative content lives at the comprehension horizon (Z1, Z9).

rows.label: A5
rows.name: Registration
rows.statement: \textbf{Registration}: every observation is an incomplete registration by a bounded proper part --- whatever reads the totality is a framed observer embedded within it (A3) and is not the whole; the totality has no frame and no reader of its own.

rows.label: A6
rows.name: Counting closes by return
rows.statement: Counting closes by return: the successor $C_q:x\mapsto x{+}1\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)$ on $q\ge2$ points is one $q$-cycle with no fixed point, so iteration is bounded and cyclic; its interpretation is A2's.

rows.label: A7
rows.name: The Carrier C
rows.statement: \textbf{The Carrier C}: A timeless torsor of $\Om$ elements, its cardinality is its only absolute characteristic; reframings $x\mapsto ax+b$ are automorphisms, so $0,1,-1$ are frame data; a Subject's frame charts it as the prime field $\F_\Om$ --- the frame's chart, never the Carrier (C1). Arena and numbers: B1.

rows.label: A8
rows.name: Scale, the sole quantitative import
rows.statement: Scale, the sole quantitative import: the de Sitter entropy of the observable universe fixes the cardinality exactly, $\Om=4\dS+1$. Its chart numeral is $\dS=\pi(r_H/\ell_P)^2=3.3\times10^{122}$ [chart] at $r_H=c/H_\Lambda$ (14-entr), so $\Om=1.3\times10^{123}$ and $\ln\Om=283.5$ [chart], the numeral of every chart reading in the ledger. The Carrier congruences are certified by the realisations (B5, C8), not imported. Metrology: L2.

rows.label: A9
rows.name: Realisation, not correspondence
rows.statement: \textbf{Realisation, not correspondence}: a sufficiently expressive, predictive, registration-complete structure \emph{is} its subject, not an abstraction of it. By the Registration pillar (A5) no registration reaches an unregistered reality, so a distinction with no registered residue is no distinction. Identification rows (\tR) are therefore constitutive: defended by the totality of registered consequences, killed by explicit falsifiers.

rows.label: A10
rows.name: The trusted base
rows.statement: \textbf{The trusted base}: the kernel's type theory, with the prelude's natural numbers read as the index of shells; no core statement asserts unboundedness, and no step of a certificate computes a count above $\Om$ at any admissible instance.

rows.label: A11
rows.name: Completeness is primality
rows.statement: \textbf{Completeness is primality}: the residues of a count $q\ge2$ have no proper nonzero ideal iff $q$ is prime, so the arithmetic of a counting cycle is complete exactly on prime cycles --- the formal shadow of A3, since a proper closed substructure of the totality would be a second totality within it.

rows.label: A12
rows.name: The quarter-turn exists iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4)
rows.statement: \textbf{The quarter-turn exists iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$}: for an odd prime $\p$, $-1$ is a square in $\F_\p$ iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ (the formal shadow of B3).

rows.label: A13
rows.name: Every prime carries a frame
rows.statement: \textbf{Every prime carries a frame}: every prime field $\F_\p$ of the totality has a primitive root, so a drive $\gen$ with $\langle\gen\rangle=\F_\p^{\times}$ exists (the formal shadow of C1).

rows.label: A14
rows.name: Labels and support
rows.statement: \textbf{Labels and support}: a reading's labels $\mathcal L_i$ count distinctions only through their support $\rho_i{:}\mathcal L_i\to\Om$; labels with one support are one distinction, so the distinctions realised are the quotient $\mathcal L_i/{\sim_i}$, and labels may outnumber them without adding one (A5).

rows.label: B1
rows.name: All numbers are unframed Carrier residues
rows.statement: All numbers are unframed Carrier residues, framed rationals ($\fQ$) in a Subject frame, in which every structure the sciences use is built exactly. The continuum is a labelled idealisation read against $\mathbb R$ [chart], never an object. The accessible smalls are the counts below the observer's horizon, the wrap-free window of primality, parity and order (B8, B9).

rows.label: B2
rows.name: Phase cycle Φ=Ω×≅CΩ-1, the split torus of order Ω-1=4S
rows.statement: Phase cycle $\Phi=\F_\Om^{\times}\cong C_{\Om-1}$, the split torus of order $\Om-1=4\dS$; the cycle's order and divisor lattice are frame-invariant (the arithmetic of $\dS$ is the spectrum of admissible dynamics), its marked elements frame data.

rows.label: B3
rows.name: Quarter-turn torsion: 4|Ω-1 by construction (Ω=4S+1
rows.statement: Quarter-turn torsion: $4\mid\Om-1$ by construction ($\Om=4\dS+1$, A8), so the split torus carries a unique order-four subgroup --- the Carrier's $Q_4$ core $\{1,\hbar,-1,h\}$ ($\hbar^2\equiv-1$, $h:=-\hbar$ the root-pair partner of $\hbar$, B7), the symmetry-complete condition. The Subject's labels $\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$ are frame data (C1), the two quarter-turns distinct objects (D7).

rows.label: B4
rows.name: Triality centre: 3|Ω+1, so the non-split torus carries a unique
rows.statement: Triality centre: $3\mid\Om+1$, so $x^2+x+1$ has no root in $\F_\Om$, and its roots $\omega,\omega^2$ with $1$ form the unique order-three group of norm-one residue pairs, the triality centre; its labels $\{1,\omega,\omega^2\}$ are Subject frame data (C1); jointly with B3 it forces the substrate residue (B5).

rows.label: B5
rows.name: The substrate residue
rows.statement: \textbf{The substrate residue}: the quarter-turn ($4\mid\Om-1$, B3) and the triality centre ($3\mid\Om+1$, B4) jointly hold iff $\Om\equiv5\pmod{12}$. Both are relations certified by realisations, never properties of an integer: $Q_4$ by the quantum realisation (D4), the triality centre by the strong realisation (D6). The inference runs structure $\to$ congruence (A3); a laboratory pattern instantiates the residue or does not (10:E9).

rows.label: B6
rows.name: Four generative levels (succession → addition → multiplication →
rows.statement: Four generative levels (succession $\to$ addition $\to$ multiplication $\to$ fixed-base exponentiation) generate the carrier's two cyclic structures ($C_\Om$, $C_{\Om-1}$) and the exponential bridge lemma; the fifth level (tetration) folds back since exponents are $(\Om{-}1)$-cardinality residues, so the hierarchy, unbounded under the classical reading, closes at four over $\F_\Om$ (structural, not a cost claim).

rows.label: B7
rows.name: Physical constants are definite Carrier residues
rows.statement: \textbf{Physical constants are definite Carrier residues}: the register $\{\dS,\Om,c,\hbar,G,k_B\}$ is generator-free in $\dS$ alone --- $G=2\dS=-c^2$, $c^2=2^{-1}$ (C8, D7), $\hbar^2=-1$, $k_B^2=-2$, $|k_B|=\hbar/c$; the defining congruences are the observer's complete certificates, $G$ exact, the rest up to sign (B10); $h:=-\hbar$ is the root-pair partner of $\hbar$ (B3, D7). No Subject counterpart of $G$ or $\hbar$; no fifth constant (C1).

rows.label: B8
rows.name: The window ladder
rows.statement: \textbf{The window ladder}: a nested Subject, $\p^2<\Om$, has its own horizon below the Carrier's quarter-root, $\sqrt\p<\Om^{1/4}$, and its shell below the coherence horizon, $\p<\Om^{1/2}$; the saturating Subject ($\p^2\to\Om$) locks the ladder $\mathrm{small}<\Om^{1/4}<\p\text{-hard}<\Om^{1/2}<\Om\text{-hard}<\Om$, one square-root horizon per embedding (the bands: B12). Lab-verified ($\Om=2{,}408{,}561$).

rows.label: B9
rows.name: Certification is the orthogonal axis
rows.statement: \textbf{Certification is the orthogonal axis} to the B8 bands: a certified entity carries a bounded-height defining relation holding across shells; a framed transcendental is a hard role with none. Registers: at the Carrier the four constants (B7); at the Subject the half-period and quarter-turn, $2\pi\equiv-1$, $\im^2\equiv-1$ (C1) --- the same congruence shapes (self-similarity). Physical constants $\Om$-hard, mathematical constants $\p $-hard.

rows.label: B10
rows.name: One gauge bit closes the sign sector
rows.statement: \textbf{One gauge bit closes the sign sector}: no C14-type marker exists --- $-1$ is a square on admissible $\Om$, so square class is pair-blind, and integer parity is frame data (A7). Registered faces are pair-invariant: $c^2$, the one-way member synchronisation gauge (C8); $|k_B|$ (C12); $\{\hbar,h\}$ the two named unit faces (B7).

rows.label: B12
rows.name: The two-level horizon law
rows.statement: \textbf{The two-level horizon law}: hardness is one mechanism at every scale --- a role is $\Om$-hard when it lives at the Carrier's scale, $\p$-hard when it lies beyond the Subject's own horizon $\sqrt\p$ inside its own shell; hardness attaches to roles, never to bare residues. The ladder: B8; certification: B9.

rows.label: B13
rows.name: The sign of the Boltzmann residue
rows.statement: \textbf{The sign of the Boltzmann residue}: $k_B:=-\hbar/c$, the sign fixed by the Hawking scaling $k_Bc=h$ read in the chart [chart]; the registered face is $|k_B|$ (B10).

rows.label: B14
rows.name: The octant sector
rows.statement: \textbf{The octant sector}: $C_8\subset C_{4\dS}$ exists exactly when $\dS$ is even (14:C6).

rows.label: C1
rows.name: The frame, Subject-only: (τ;0,1,g)
rows.statement: The frame, Subject-only: $(\chron;0,1,\gen)$, origin, unit and the drive $x\mapsto gx$ (A7). Shell data, capacity-first: $\kap $ primitive, $\p =4\kap +1$, $\im=-\gen^\kap $ (C7), $\pi=2\kap $, $e=\gen^{\,\im}$; $\gen$ the one nonsquare frame datum (C3, C8). Exponents of $\gen$ are taken in $\Zp$, a residue in an exponent standing for its lift $\iota:\F_\p\to\{0,\dots,\p-1\}$. The web closes on every shell: $2\pi\equiv-1$, $\gen^{\,\pi}\equiv-1$, $-\pi=2^{-1}$ (N2).

rows.label: C2
rows.name: Scale-shift duality: dilation xgx is phase evolution of the frame
rows.statement: Scale-shift duality: dilation $x\mapsto gx$ is phase evolution of the frame, advancing $t$; over the cycle it is the fractional Fourier transform, whose quarter-turn $Q_4$ is the discrete Fourier transform.

rows.label: C3
rows.name: Euclidean--Lorentzian dichotomy
rows.statement: The drive fixes a Lorentzian time axis, causal order is algebraic, the split and non-split tori the two signatures. The signature is the square class of the temporal coefficient $\nu=\gen$ (C1); in $\F_\p$, $\nu=2^{-1}\cdot(2\gen)$, both classes fixed by the parity of $\kap$ (8:B3). In the Carrier $c^2=2^{-1}$ is a square (C8, D7), and $\eta_{00}=-c^2$ is a chart artifact.

rows.label: C4
rows.name: Observer = embedded shell (frame)
rows.statement: Observer $=$ embedded shell (frame); observation $=$ shared-core comparison of two phase cycles.

rows.label: C5
rows.name: Oriented frame = unimodular basis
rows.statement: Oriented frame $=$ unimodular basis; two oriented frames differ by exactly one matrix of determinant one.

rows.label: C6
rows.name: One frame group, three sectors
rows.statement: Gravity's $(3{+}1)$ tensor, the Riemann observer geometry and the quantum spinor structure are three readings of a shell's frame group $\mathrm{SL}_2$ (C22), element by element, its three tori the scale-time, translation and boost freedoms; continuum shadow the declared $S^3$ (C23), spinor double cover the Clifford layer (D4). Falsifier: a registered space-time, observer or spinor freedom outside the three tori.

rows.label: C7
rows.name: Orientation is derived, not conventional
rows.statement: \textbf{Orientation is derived, not conventional}: the $c$-square congruence ($\dS$ even, C8) annihilates orientation transport on every Carrier carrying it ($\im^{\dS}\in\{\pm1\}$); the oriented quarter-turn $\im=-\gen^\kap $ is a selection, read by pullback covariance and count positivity; the joint flip $(\gen,\im,s)\mapsto(\gen^{-1},-\im,-s)$ permutes the registration channels. The constants' derivation consumes no selection (B7). Parity marker: C14. The selection by matter content: D16.

rows.label: C8
rows.name: The square class is chronon parity
rows.statement: For a primitive drive the squares are $\langle \gen^2\rangle$: a residue's quadratic class is its drive-step parity. Registered transport is even, the one-way multiplier $\gen$ odd, so the one-way speed is gauge and the two-way constant invariant. $[c^2]$ is even iff $\dS$ is even, a relation certified by the unit realisation (D7). The Tsirelson $\sqrt2=\zeta_8+\zeta_8^{-1}$ is its two-way symmetrisation.

rows.label: C9
rows.name: The Object frame is (t,q,k,v)
rows.statement: \textbf{The Object frame is $(\dt;\,q,k,v)$}: every entry a Subject residue --- offset $\dt$ (synchronisation datum), position $q$, winding $k$ (D2), rate $v$; one relative datum per frame datum. The momentum reading is one quarter-turn from the winding, $p=\im\,k$; the canonical commutator $[\hat q,\hat p]=\im\hbar$ composes the Subject's chart quarter-turn with the Carrier's action quantum (D7, B7).

rows.label: C10
rows.name: Two strata of probability
rows.statement: A registered probability is a framed rational; a structural weight is an element of the parity-even cyclotomic subring. The strata coincide exactly on the stationary core-valued $Q_4$ sector, joined by two proved reductions and the stratum-sampling clause (D10). On a single Object the weights are uniform over the fibres (22-qm Rem.~borndomain); non-uniform statistics arrive through the engineered-core readout.

rows.label: C11
rows.name: Pair-tally uniqueness
rows.statement: \textbf{Pair-tally uniqueness} (22-qm Prop.~gleason, the uniqueness of the pair tally on the stationary $Q_4$ sector): on the stationary core-valued $Q_4$ sector, tally-valued, fibre-additive, drive-invariant, parity-even registration functionals form the character cone fixed by the pure windings; adding channel-selectivity (assumed, not derived; the sampling clause D10) picks the Born ray. The minimal degree is forced; proof shape: 22-qm.

rows.label: C12
rows.name: Temperature and the classical arity, derived
rows.statement: \textbf{Temperature and the classical arity, derived}: the temperature domain is acceleration, $[\Theta]=[E][k_B]^{-1}=[L][T]^{-2}$, flag-free, $\Theta_P=E_P/|k_B|$, Unruh closing as a domain identity; neither mass nor temperature is primitive --- $M$-$L$-$T$-plus-thermal is the torsion-free shadow of the two-generators-plus-flag system (the mass primitive standing in for the flag, the thermal for $k_B$), classical dimensional analysis recovered in exponents and arity.

rows.label: C14
rows.name: The quarter-turn is the odd member of the ±√-1 pair
rows.statement: \textbf{The quarter-turn is the odd member of the $\pm\sqrt{-1}$ pair}: the two representatives have opposite integer parity (distinct from chronon parity, C8), and $e^{\,\im\pi}:=\gen^{\,2\kap\,\iota(\im)^{2}}\equiv(-1)^{\iota(\im)}$ (the lift $\iota$ of C1), so $e^{\,\im\pi}\equiv-1$ holds exactly on the odd member. The conjugate chart toggles it: the parity names the matter--antimatter gauge (C7), and the selection is generator-independent within the chirality.

rows.label: C16
rows.name: The spinor dichotomy
rows.statement: \textbf{The spinor dichotomy}: $\kap$ odd $\Leftrightarrow$ $C_{\p-1}\cong C_4\times C_\kap$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $v_2(\p-1)=2$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $3\kap r+4s\equiv1\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 4\kap)$ is solvable: the spinor class. Shell and Carrier share the $2$-part $C_{2^m}$, $m=\min(v_2(\p-1),v_2(\Om-1))$, and the shell closes on a cover of degree $2^{v_2(\Om-1)-m}$; the shared order times the cover degree is the Carrier's $2$-part, $8$ exactly when $\dS\equiv2\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 4)$. The midpoint event of a $\kap$-odd shell: C18.

rows.label: C18
rows.name: The precession theorem
rows.statement: \textbf{The precession theorem}: over the pair dynamics the shell orbit precesses against the Carrier quarter by the winding ratio (D2): the apsidal fraction per revolution is exactly $\kap /\dS =(\p -1)/(\Om -1)$, every $\kap$-odd pair with the $c$-square ($\dS$ even, C8); the half event (home, dlog$(-1)$) sits at the exact midpoint, closure at (home, home); orientation prograde, Subject-selected (C14, the gauge bit).

rows.label: C19
rows.name: The Hopf section
rows.statement: \textbf{The Hopf section}: on the frames by elements (no group counted, Q20) the boost torus $C_{\p +1}$ is fixed-point-free on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and meets the Borel trivially, so every frame factors uniquely as (cone-chart event)$\times$(boost): the cone chart is a global section of the non-split fibration (C22), $\p (\p -1)$ fibres of $\p +1$; $\mathrm{SL}_2$ obstructs at $-1$.

rows.label: C20
rows.name: The mass--energy channel
rows.statement: \textbf{The mass--energy channel}: the winding sector $C_{\p -1}$ meets the boost base $C_{\p +1}$ in the sign alone and the spinor cover $C_{2(\p +1)}$ in exactly $Q_4$, every $\p =4\kap +1$; the quarter is spinorial, $N(\im)=\im^{2}=-1$: the mass transport crosses the sheet; mass phase $=$ winding rate, one $Q_4$ datum (D2); Carrier instance $78^{58}=89=h$ on $\Om =233$ (38:A4).

rows.label: C21
rows.name: The dilation rigidity theorem
rows.statement: \textbf{The dilation rigidity theorem}: static clock comparison is a register character $\gen^{-\Delta n}$; characters are rigid, so the strong-field dilation law is the unique exponential reading, zero coefficient freedom; the PPN temporal form admits no register character (transitivity defect exactly $4ab$); the cover halves the angle at every tick (C20).

rows.label: C22
rows.name: The frame variety and its two fibrations
rows.statement: $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\F_\p)\cong\mathrm{SO}_3(\F_\p)$, and the norm-one sphere is $\mathrm{SL}_2$, the spin cover of its rotation half $\mathrm{PSL}_2$. For every $\p=4\kap+1$ of the totality each frame is uniquely one direction in $\mathbb{P}^1$, one shell cell and one drive phase. Two fibrations partition the frames: non-split $C_{\p +1}$ over $\p (\p -1)$, with the cone-chart section (C19); split $C_{\p -1}$ over $\p (\p +1)$, with no subgroup section.

rows.label: C23
rows.name: The spatial chart is the 3-sphere (declared)
rows.statement: $SU(2)=S^3$ is declared the continuum chart of the frame group (C27) [chart]. The group has the three element types of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, $SU(2)$ only one; no finite datum marks the compact real form, and cycle closure selects none. Then the spinor sign gives $S^3$, not $SO(3)$ (C22), uniqueness is Poincar\'e--Perelman [import], and de Sitter slicing has $S^3$ sections [import] (A8).

rows.label: C24
rows.name: The third-order wall of π
rows.statement: \textbf{The third-order wall of $\pi$}: for every prime $\p\ge5$ of the totality, $\sigma_\p=\sum_{k<(\p-1)/2}\binom{2k}{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})$ satisfies $\sigma_\p\equiv0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{2})$ (Sun, JNT \textbf{131} (2011), (1.4)) and $\sigma_\p/\p^{2}\equiv(-1)^{(\p+1)/2}B_{\p-3}/36\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p)$: Sun's Conjecture 5.1, $\sigma_\p\equiv(-1)^{(\p-1)/2}(H_{\p-1}/12+3\p^{4}B_{\p-5}/160)\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{5})$ for $\p>5$, proved by Hessami Pilehrood, Hessami Pilehrood and Tauraso (Int.\ J.\ Number Theory \textbf{8} (2012), Thm.\ 5 (44)), reduced mod $\p^{3}$ with Glaisher's $H_{\p-1}\equiv-\p^{2}B_{\p-3}/3\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{3})$; $\p=5$ direct. Re-verified for all primes below $10^{4}$.

rows.label: C25
rows.name: The horizon is the origin's antipode on the boost torus
rows.statement: For $w^2=\nu$ a nonsquare, the torsor map $\mathbb{P}^1(\F_\p)\to C_{\p +1}$, $P\mapsto u_P/\bar u_P$ with $u_P$ the unique boost carrying $0$ to $P$, is equivariant and sends the origin to $1$ and the horizon $[1{:}0]$ to $-1=\zeta^{(\p +1)/2}$. Origin and horizon are the sign pair $C_{\p -1}\cap C_{\p +1}$ (C20), exchanged by the torus's unique involution $q\mapsto\nu/q$. On the additive cycle the antipode is the seam $\p/2$ (1:Z1, 1:Z2).

rows.label: C26
rows.name: The four chains of 13-epi are E- and G-partial sums
rows.statement: The derangement chain $D_n/n!=\sum_{k\le n}(-1)^{k}/k!$ is the partial-sum chain of the E-function $e^{-z}$ at $1$; the arcsin and Machin chains are those of the G-functions $\arcsin z$ at $1/2$ and $\arctan z$ at $1/5$, $1/239$; $e^{\pm1}\in\mathcal E$ and $\pi,1/\pi\in\mathcal G$, both rings (Fischler--Rivoal) [import]. The factorial rate $\Theta(k/\log k)$ against the geometric rate $\Theta(k)$ of 13-epi E5 is that of E- against G-partial sums.

rows.label: C27
rows.name: The frame group has one form
rows.statement: \textbf{The frame group has one form}: on every shell $\mathrm{SU}_2(\F_{\p^2}/\F_\p)=\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\p)$ for the Hermitian form $wJ$, $w^{\p}=-w$, every element of finite order; the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2=1$ and $ad-bc=1$ correspond point by point through the quarter-turn.

rows.label: D1
rows.name: Time is scale-dilation
rows.statement: Each Subject's clock is its own drive $x\mapsto gx$. A composite is read through the reader's one drive, so its diagonal action and conserved offset are observer-derived, the offset group fixed by the arena's divisor structure; the Carrier has no clock. Falsifier: a registered duration that is not a drive count of the reader's frame, or a frame-independent Carrier tick.

rows.label: D2
rows.name: Mass is winding rate (E=hf an identity)
rows.statement: \textbf{Mass is winding rate} ($E=hf$ an identity); masslessness $\Leftrightarrow$ drive-invariance; a mass is the non-split component the drive rotates, the part of a residue pair that Frobenius conjugation reverses, masslessness the split-torus eigen-alignment. Falsifier: a rest mass with no cycle winding, a massless drive-variant state, or a stationary state whose registered frequency is not its winding index ($E=hf$ failing).

rows.label: D3
rows.name: Distance is decoherence
rows.statement: \textbf{Distance is decoherence}: the separation of two systems is their decoherence count in the observer's chart, the metric the graph metric of shared-core comparison --- the spatial reading of the one relational channel, the twin of D1 (time) and D2 (mass). Falsifier: a metric separation not monotone in the decoherence count of the relational channel.

rows.label: D4
rows.name: Quantum: matter is the phase character of a finite cycle
rows.statement: \textbf{Quantum}: matter is the phase character of a finite cycle; observation is shared-core comparison; the complex amplitude is forced by $Q_4$ ($\im^2{=}{-}1$). Falsifier: a confirmed third-order interference $I_3\neq0$, $S\neq2\sqrt2$, or real-amplitude network behaviour (22-qm P2, P3).

rows.label: D5
rows.name: Gravity: a cell-local change of frame is a gauge symmetry
rows.statement: \textbf{Gravity}: a cell-local change of frame is a gauge symmetry, and the connection compensating it is the field (the geometric/diffeomorphism frame). Falsifier: a source gravitating by other than its full mass, entanglement induced off the Newtonian rate, or $\eta\neq0$ (22-qm P1, C22).

rows.label: D6
rows.name: Forces: the same recipe applied to the substrate's three other
rows.statement: \textbf{Forces}: the same recipe applied to the substrate's three \emph{other} frame data, namely phase (EM), spinor (weak), and colour (strong); ``finish gauging the frame.'' Falsifier: a fifth force, a gauge group or charge outside the rank-five frame, or a fourth generation.

rows.label: D7
rows.name: A unit of measure is a reciprocal cross-frame relation
rows.statement: A unit is observer counts per substrate count, its atomic form the action quantum $\hbar^2=-1$ (B7), its domain the unit-free order-four flag: unitful measures carry it, observables are flag-free, the absolute unit value $\Om$-hard. The fundamental units are the four domain horizons (10-dim). Falsifier: an embedded observer registering an absolute unit value, or a unitful measure with no cross-frame reciprocal.

rows.label: D8
rows.name: Elementary is Ω-hard
rows.statement: \textbf{Elementary is $\Om$-hard}: an elementary particle is a large beyond-horizon residue, never observed at rest; the observable exception is the gauge sector's drive-invariant residue, the photon (G1, Z6); instantiated at $517\times\sqrt\Om$ on a concrete shell (37-sim). Falsifier: an elementary particle with a resolved internal residue (substructure), or a massive drive-invariant gauge residue.

rows.label: D9
rows.name: The observable is a small residue
rows.statement: \textbf{The observable is a small residue}: a bounded observer reads only small residues, so an observable stable object carries a small exact residue (particle $+$ binding wrap) --- the confined hadron, the light nucleus, the stable atom; decay is frame-normalisation toward it. Falsifier: a stable observable object carrying no small exact residue --- a stable coloured state, or strong/electromagnetic proton decay.

rows.label: D10
rows.name: The unified sampling clause
rows.statement: A registration protocol samples one stratum of a drive-presented ensemble. Over complete joint recurrences the counts are forced exact tallies (22-qm Rem.~strata), on incomplete batches the largest-remainder gauge, shared by the quantum readout and the gravity crossover. rows.statement: RH, Goldbach, and P-vs-NP are the spectral, additive, and computational faces of one horizon clause: each a uniform check over the totality whose per-instance statements are $\Om$-blind relations (RH: Z10, Z11) and whose uniform form is an $\Om$-hard value (Z3, Z4), host-decided on a hosted Carrier. An $\Om$-hard value says nothing about whether a bounded-height certificate exists.

rows.label: Z3
rows.name: The bounded-observer certificate for each is Ω-hard (Z4)
rows.statement: The bounded-observer certificate for each is $\Om$-hard (Z4): the completed uniform check over all residues of the totality, in no embedded reader's window. $\Om$-hardness is the absence of a host; on a hosted shell the same check is host-decided (37-sim; D8). Within capacity an embedded observer decides totality-level facts from internal state (two-record keystone): the horizon has two operational sides.

rows.label: Z4
rows.name: The three certificates: RH = the on-line spectrum complete
rows.statement: RH $=$ the on-line spectrum complete for the prime vector; Goldbach $=$ the uniform per-$n$ parity positivity; P-vs-NP $=$ the forward-invertibility of the scale descent. Each is a uniform check over the totality, in no embedded reader's window; the per-instance statements are $\Om$-blind relations (Z10, Z11). Whether a certificate exists is undecided (20-rh \S8.3).

rows.label: Z5
rows.name: The horizon forces structure, not only leaves it open
rows.statement: The horizon \emph{forces} structure, not only leaves it open: the $3+2$ split is beyond the horizon (above $\sqrt{\Om}$), so the off-block reframings are gauge and unification is the simple $\SO(10)$ (G14); the automorphism lemma reduces to the Registration pillar (A5).

rows.label: Z6
rows.name: The sixteen's absolute masses are Ω-hard framed-transcendentals
rows.statement: The sixteen's absolute masses are $\Om$-hard framed-transcendentals, the matter face of the horizon clause (Z2--Z4). Value tagged: the absolute masses (G13), in no embedded reader's window; the relations among them (G16--G18) are $\Om$-blind. Classification ``elementary $=$ beyond-horizon'' is D8; the $\mathbf{16}\to$spectrum projection is G18; the gauge sector's drive-invariant residue (the photon, residue $2$) is the above-horizon, observable complement (D8, G1).

rows.label: Z7
rows.name: The dark sector's cross-scale running is the cosmological face
rows.statement: The dark sector's cross-scale running is the \emph{cosmological} face of the horizon clause. Value tagged: the running's absolute normalisation, $a_0$ at one epoch in physical units, equivalently the absolute scale of $H$, in no embedded reader's window; its uniform certificate is the factorisation of $\Om-1$, shared with Z2--Z4, Z6 and Z8. The \emph{shape} $a_0(z)\propto H(z)$ is a relation, not $\Om$-hard (P1).

rows.label: Z8
rows.name: The fine-structure constant is the electromagnetic face
rows.statement: The fine-structure constant is the \emph{electromagnetic} face of the scale operator: $\alpha^{-1}(0)=4\pi+\sum_f\tfrac{b_f}{2\pi}\ln(M_P/m_f)+\Delta\alpha_{\mathrm{had}}$, $\Om$-hard --- the bare $1/4\pi$ framed-exact (the Gauss solid angle), the digit a log over the $\Om$-hard masses (Z6) with cutoff $M_P$ tied to $\Om$ (A8). The physical digit is in no embedded reader's window; the bare value and the sum's form are $\Om$-blind. Of the family Z2/Z6/Z7/G3/G6.

rows.label: Z9
rows.name: No compression
rows.statement: \textbf{No compression}: the diagonal has no instance per symbol (25:F2), nor, coded a base-$a$ digit per symbol, from length $t(\M)=d\,k^{*}(\M)<|\M|$ on (25:F6). Below $t(\M)$, decoders over $(\F_\p,+,\times)$ give one coded 1024 base-32 symbols per element, more than $\Om$'s elements hold (25:F7, 25:F8, A8). There fragment truth is definable from above (the Tarski reversal, 25:G5), and not from far below (25:G8).

rows.label: Z10
rows.name: The shell theorem
rows.statement: On every shell $\F_\p\subset\F_{\p^2}$, with no hypothesis, the prime vector's spectral content is the constant mode and the nonterminal quarter-turn modes, the finite zeta vanishing on each (20:E12, 20:B4). Every mode of every vector lies on the self-dual line $\Tr=1$, an eigenvector of the scale-shift with a $(\p-1)$-th root of unity as eigenvalue: no off-line mode, $\Om$-blind.

rows.label: Z11
rows.name: The classical hypothesis is a screen value
rows.statement: RH below height $T$ is the count identity $\mathcal N(T)=N_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)$, $C\le N_{\mathrm{crit}}\le\mathcal N$ [import: Turing 1953], a screen value (20:F1--F4), both counts read from the explicit formula's two sides, inputs frame-exact, outputs uncertified. An off-line zero is a phantom, a comb count with no on-line mode (20:A5). Decidable per height; uniform form Z4. Falsifier: a shell window where $\mathcal N-N_{\mathrm{crit}}$ differs from Turing's count.
